draft.title: Chromatography
card: Chromatography separates a mixture of dissolved substances, such as the dyes in an ink. It works well on small amounts of a mixture.
A spot of the mixture is placed near the bottom of a strip of paper. The bottom edge is stood in a solvent, such as water. The spot must start above the level of the solvent.
The solvent soaks up the paper and carries the dissolved substances with it. Each substance travels a different distance, so the substances spread out into separate spots or bands.
A substance that is carried further up the paper has moved faster than one that stays lower down. A pure substance usually gives one spot. A mixture gives more than one.
draft.remember: In chromatography, the solvent carries each substance a different distance up the paper.

a.q: Why does chromatography separate the dyes in a black ink into different spots?
opts: Each dye is carried a different distance by the solvent
Each dye dissolves in the paper and stays there
Each dye evaporates from the paper at its own time
Each dye is too large to pass through the paper
a.why: The solvent moves up the paper and carries each dye with it, but each dye travels a different distance. This spreads them into separate spots. The dyes are not trapped by the paper, because they are carried along by the solvent.
a.clue: Think about what moves up the paper and how far each dye goes.

b.q: Priya tests a green ink on paper. After the solvent has risen, she sees a yellow spot near the top and a blue spot lower down. What does this show?
opts: The ink is a mixture of at least two dyes
The ink is a single pure dye
The blue dye is carried faster than the yellow dye
The solvent has made the ink change colour
b.why: Two separate spots mean the ink contains at least two different dyes, so it is a mixture. The yellow dye was carried further, so it moved faster than the blue dye, which is the reverse of the tempting option.
b.clue: Count the spots, then compare how far each one has travelled.

wants.brief: A strip of paper standing in a beaker with a little solvent in the bottom. A start line with a spot of ink sits above the solvent level. A second strip shows the solvent front near the top and three separate coloured spots at different heights, labelled spot 1, spot 2 and spot 3.
wants.why: Seeing the setup and the spread-out spots helps students understand how each substance travels a different distance.

a.best: Each dye is carried a different distance by the solvent

b.best: The ink is a mixture of at least two dyes
